lots.title: Provision of Water Risk Assessments (Legionella Survey)
lots.description: Lot 2 of the London Borough of Bexley Building Services Framework 6278. Single-lot Specification ('Schedule 1') for the provision of Water Risk Assessments / Legionella Surveys across the Council's operational estate, commencing April 2026 for a period of 3 + 2 years. The Supplier (Contractor) provides all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources to deliver Water Management Surveys that enable, support and evidence the Council's statutory compliance obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, the Approved Code of Practice (ACOP) L8, HSE Guidance HSG 274 Parts 1-3 and BSI 8580:2010. Core services include Water Hygiene Assessments of hot and cold water systems (mains distribution, stored water tanks, calorifiers and outlets), production of site Water Hygiene Management Plans, monitoring programmes (temperature checks, flushing, inspection regimes), annual review of WRAs, production of risk-rated (high / medium / low) electronic reports within ten (10) days of each inspection with 48-hour high-priority remedial notifications, consolidation of remedial works into a RAG-rated programme of works in Microsoft Excel via the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud / Civica), operative training in Legionella control, Water Management awareness training for Council staff and partners, and specialist advice on ACOP L8 compliance. The Contractor must operate a Dynamic Risk Assessment process prior to any planned or reactive works. The schedule of buildings and indicative volumes is governed by Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix; environmental obligations by Appendix C; and the Code of Conduct by Appendix D.
requirements: Provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources for the undertaking of Legionella Surveys / Water Risk Assessments (section 1).

Provide a named representative to oversee the provision of the Service and work with the Council and the Service Manager to develop and improve the Services within the scope and financial limits of the Contract (section 1).

Conduct Water Risk Assessments as instructed, ensuring a high-quality service in line with this Specification and the Contract, respecting site-specific requirements that may differ across Sites and building types (section 2).

In collaboration with the Council, prepare an annual schedule of Water Risk Assessments aligned with this Specification and Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix, submit for Council approval, and indicate whether each activity is a statutory compliance requirement or a best practice service (section 2).

If asbestos is discovered or suspected, immediately cease work, notify the Council, and not disturb or remove any Asbestos Containing Material without Council agreement and full compliance with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012; consult and sign the site-specific Asbestos Risk Management Plan and register before commencing any work (section 2).

Agree access and security arrangements for each Site during mobilisation (including any necessary alarm-setting training), maintain the Council's key handover and return system, nominate a key-holder, provide 24-hour access contact details in writing to the FM Team, and report loss or misplacement of Keys immediately (section 2).
Reimburse the Council for all costs arising from lost or damaged Keys, including lock changes, door/gate replacements and security-system reprogramming (section 2).

Ensure all Employees comply with the No-Smoking designation covering all Sites and external areas; do not move Council equipment, furniture or specialist items unless expressly authorised (section 2).
Comply fully with the Approved Code of Practice (ACOP) L8 for the control of Legionella bacteria in water systems, HSE Guidance HSG 274 Parts 1-3, and BSI 8580:2010 (section 3).

Inspect the hygiene conditions of hot and cold water systems across all contracted sites, including mains distribution, stored water tanks, calorifiers and outlets (wash hand basins, showers), as outlined in the Building List (Appendix A) (section 3).

Produce a Water Hygiene Assessment report per site within ten (10) days of inspection, containing a summary of assessed risks, an executive summary, site details, schematic drawings of all water systems, risk estimation methodology, photographic evidence, and clear recommendations with risks categorised as high / medium / low (section 3).

Report any immediate risks to the FM Team while the inspector is still on site and communicate any high-priority remedial work to the FM Team via email within 48 hours of the inspection, prior to formal report submission (section 3).

Provide all monitoring and reporting documents electronically through the CAFM system (TF Cloud) or by email until system integration is complete; produce the consolidated prioritised remedial works programme (RAG-rated) in Microsoft Excel from the start of the contract and update it monthly (section 3).

Maintain a site-specific Water Hygiene Management Plan for each location incorporating WRA findings, with control measures, monitoring regimes and responsibilities; implement a proactive monitoring programme (temperature checks, flushing regimes, inspection of tanks and calorifiers, biocide dosing where applicable); review WRAs annually or sooner if there are significant changes to water systems, occupancy or usage (section 3).
Ensure all operatives involved in water hygiene management are trained in Legionella control procedures, hold relevant certifications, and submit training records to the Council annually (section 3).

Identify and report any areas of perceived or actual risk to Bexley's compliance with regulations and ACOPs, recommending remedial actions; review the adequacy of existing risk assessments and advise on updates or revisions (section 3).
Submit sample documentation demonstrating all site-report, RAG, schematic, photographic and methodology requirements with the bid (section 3).

Use the Council's Asset Management System (TF Cloud / Civica) to record job completion, upload documentation, and process payment applications; attend provided training; no invoices accepted outside this system; no further claims accepted after an invoice has been raised (section 4).
Quote the system-generated reference number issued with each statutory compliance inspection instruction in all communications with the Council regarding that job (section 4).

Carry out all statutory inspections in accordance with the standards specified by the Council; the schedule of buildings where inspections may be instructed is detailed in Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix (section 4).

Comply with all applicable health and safety legislation, including the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and all relevant statutory provisions, codes of practice and HSE Good Practice Guidance Notes; promptly advise the Council of any areas of non-compliance and obtain prior written approval for any remedial works (section 5).

Provide all necessary equipment and safe power provision; formally train all operatives in the safe use of tools and supply appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE); maintain comprehensive training and assessment records and submit them to the Council annually (section 5).

Ensure all operatives and staff are familiar with the Council's emergency evacuation procedures for each building; assume the presence of asbestos-containing materials in plant rooms and appliances unless proven otherwise (section 5).

Submit a Risk Assessment and Method Statement (RAMS) for Council approval prior to commencing any works on site, covering all Services detailed in the Specification; maintain and update Workplace Risk Assessments covering both Contractor and Council work areas; keep them accessible to the Council (section 5).
Designate a single point of contact for professional health and safety advice and report all near misses and RIDDOR-reportable incidents to the Council (section 5).

Undertake the 'Authorised Person' duties required under Health and Safety regulations and complete a Dynamic Risk Assessment before any planned or reactive works, uploading it to the CAFM system (TF Cloud) per the process agreed during mobilisation (section 6).

Adhere to the Council's Environmental Policy (Appendix C) where possible, reduce the Borough's Carbon Emissions, support the Council's Social Value objectives, and submit details of the Contractor's Company Environmental Policy with illustrations and any current experience or initiatives in this field (section 7).

Provide Water Management awareness training courses for Council staff and suppliers, train and inform the Council and partners in relation to existing and future changes in Regulation and duties under ACOP L8, and provide specialist advice on all matters relating to ACOP L8 (section 8).

Provide a detailed organisational structure (escalation routes, roles and responsibilities) during mobilisation; ensure staff competence and adequate cover for absence; senior staff must have excellent English verbal and written communication skills; all staff (including subcontractors) must be DBS-checked with records available on request; Council may require removal and replacement of underperforming staff within five (5) working days (section 9).

Ensure day-to-day operational matters are managed by a designated competent resource in addition to an appointed Contract Manager; adhere to Council staffing policies; sign and adhere to a Council-agreed confidentiality policy; follow sign-in/out procedures; carry company-issued identification at all times on Council premises (section 9).

Obtain Council prior approval for any sub-contracting; retain full responsibility for subcontracted performance; vet all sub-contractors (including DBS); flow down contractual performance standards; monitor via KPIs, spot-checks and regular management meetings (section 10).

Immediately refer all complaints to the FM Client Unit, rectify service-failure complaints within SLA timeframes, log all complaints, notify the Contract Administrator within 24 hours with full details and corrective actions, and respond promptly and professionally to ensure satisfactory resolution (section 11).

Treat all users (Council Members, Representatives and stakeholders) promptly, courteously and effectively; implement a formal complaints procedure submitted as part of the tender; submit a schedule of all complaints and actions taken to the Authorised Officer at monthly operational meetings (section 12).

During mobilisation, configure all necessary IT and reporting systems; agree report format and content; establish meeting and reporting schedule; finalise the Water Risk Assessment programme of work; confirm KPIs; present all initialisation documents and files at the mobilisation meeting; agree any revised regimes via the Contract Change Mechanism (section 13).

Proactively propose new technologies, materials and methods that support greater efficiency, improved service outcomes and better value for money, in support of the Council's commitment to continuous improvement (section 14).
